rationale:
bugs_open/223 PHASE 2 — the write path finally emits the two Go kinds the schema and the reader have always expected. Phase 1 (council 495df717, APPROVED, live and proven on v1.0.1279/1283) made the index HONEST about what it cannot see; it deliberately did not make it see more. This is the second half, submitted as its own round because its blast radius is the CORPUS, not the rendering.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG. internal/analysis/analyse.go walks f.Decls and takes *ast.FuncDecl plus *ast.GenDecl ONLY when d.Tok == token.TYPE. token.VAR and token.CONST are dropped at that switch, analysis.Output has no field to carry them, and code_symbols_actions.go therefore has nothing to write. Meanwhile code_symbols' own CHECK constraint permits 'var' and 'const' (verified: kind = ANY (ARRAY['func','method','struct','interface','alias','type','var','const'])) and diagnose_code_lookup's codeKindList already treats both as CODE for its doc/code split. The schema expected them, the reader expected them, only the writer was behind. THIS IS AN UNFINISHED WRITE PATH, NOT A DESIGN GAP — which is why it is not RFC-scope: it makes the mechanism's stated guarantee ('Go symbols at the last pushed tip') true for two more kinds rather than changing its direction.

WHAT IT COSTS TODAY, both instances measured and recorded rather than argued. (1) The landmine-verifier, asked about `metaCommentaryPatterns` — a live `var` at validate_page_content.go:1229, unrenamed and not inlined — answered 'no longer resolves as a standalone symbol (possibly inlined or renamed)'. The phrasing manufactures a hypothesis the evidence never supported, and a session would act on it. (2) A 090 diagnosis run (e952039b, filed as bugs_open/231) stopped at UNVERIFIABLE with its stated gap being 'the actual var declaration of DeployImageAssetInputSpec — specifically its Defaults map — is NOT in the bundle. The content search for the identifier only surfaced its two USE sites … never the literal spec definition.' Both are one gap: every USE of a package-level value is findable and the DECLARATION is not. The diagnosis loop is therefore structurally unable to CONFIRM any hypothesis whose deciding evidence is the CONTENT of a package-level var — a spec's Defaults, a pattern table, a policy map — and it stops at UNVERIFIABLE naming exactly what it cannot see.

THE LINE SPAN IS THE DESIGN, not the name. code_symbols slices `body` from the recorded span, and for a value the body IS the evidence. A span covering only the identifier would index the name and lose the thing anyone needs. So: the SPEC's span, except for a lone unparenthesised declaration where the DECL's span is used, so the keyword and doc comment are inside the slice. In a parenthesised block the decl span covers every member, so slicing it per member would repeat the whole block once per name — hence the split, and a test pins both halves.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN EARLIER FIGURES, because both were carried into phase 1's paperwork. My first sizing was `grep -rhE "^(var|const) "` → 930, which undercounts: a grouped block counts once however many specs it holds. A design pass corrected that to 1,173 by an awk over block members. BOTH ARE WRONG. Built with the real analyser and run over this tree: var=795, const=576, TOTAL 1,371 new entries across 811 files. That is the figure to use, and the method is the point — a count of declaration TEXT is a proxy; running the parser that will actually emit the rows is the measurement.

SCOPE NOTE ON THAT FIGURE, stated so nobody reads it as a DB delta: the analyser sees 811 files where the indexed corpus covers 682 paths, so index_code_symbols applies exclusions this count does not. The DB growth will be somewhat below 1,371 — roughly +20-23% on 5,837. I have not claimed an exact post-index number because I cannot measure one until the indexer runs; the post-run census is in the acceptance steps.

NO EXISTING ROW CHANGES. content_hash is computed from composeSymbolContent(kind, symbol, signature, doc, path) and this change adds rows without touching any existing one, so the 5,837 existing embeddings are NOT recomputed — only the new rows need embedding, and embedding failure is already non-fatal and reported. Identity is (repo, path, symbol): Go forbids two package-level declarations of one name in a package, method rows are stored receiver-qualified, so no collision is introduced. The blank identifier is SKIPPED for exactly this reason — `var _ Iface = (*T)(nil)` appears several times in one file, every one would collide on UPSERT, and all but one would silently vanish.

THE PRUNE INTERLOCK, read in the code rather than assumed, and the answer is the OPPOSITE of what phase 1's design pass expected. prune_floor.go's ratio() states 'An empty cohort has nothing to lose, so it reads as fully confirmed rather than as 0/0 — a new class appearing for the first time must never be able to refuse a prune', so the FIRST run with var/const rows is safe by construction. The real exposure is the reverse and it is a mixed-fleet window: an OLD binary indexing against a DB that ALREADY holds var rows sees cohort kind=var at 0% confirmed, is Below the floor, and sets Allowed=false — refusing the WHOLE prune. That direction is safe (nothing is deleted), self-healing (the next run on the new image confirms them), and visible (a prune-refusal note). It is named here rather than discovered later.

plan.summary: Emit package-level var and const from the analyser and write them as code_symbols rows, so the index can answer about a DECLARATION and not only its use sites. Three small edits plus tests: a ValueDef type, a token.VAR/token.CONST arm on the existing GenDecl switch with spec-level line spans (the body IS the evidence for a value), and one loop in the write path using kinds already present in the CHECK constraint and in the reader's codeKindList. Additive: no existing row, hash or embedding changes. Measured with the real parser: 1,371 new entries (var=795, const=576).

edits.rationale: The contract has ONE source of truth here by design (the package doc says so), so the carrier must be declared here rather than in a consumer. `Values` is additive and `omitempty`, so an older consumer of this JSON is unaffected and an older analyser's output still unmarshals as an empty slice. Type is the DECLARED type only, empty when inferred: this package parses and does not type-check, and a guessed type rendered into a signature would be exactly the confident-wrong-answer class bugs_open/223 exists to remove.

The whole defect is one missing arm on an existing switch. Spans are spec-level inside a parenthesised block (the decl span covers every member, so slicing it per member would repeat the block once per name) and decl-level for a lone declaration (so the keyword and doc comment land inside the slice and the body reads as source). The blank identifier is skipped: it is not addressable, and since code_symbols' identity is (repo, path, symbol) every `var _` in a file would collide on UPSERT and all but one would silently vanish.

One loop beside the existing Functions and Types loops, using the same symbolRow shape, the same composeSymbolContent and the same body slicer — so nothing new is invented and the row is byte-shaped like its siblings. The kinds need no schema change: both are already in code_symbols_kind_check and in diagnose_code_lookup's codeKindList, so a var row is already treated as code (not as a [doc] row) by the reader that will consume it. The signature slot carries `var Name Type` when the source declares one, which makes a listing legible without opening the body.

Pure-function tests in the package's own style, each pinning one property that would otherwise fail silently in production. The span tests are the load-bearing ones because the span is the design: a block's members must not share one span (or every member's body is the whole block) and a lone declaration must include its keyword (or the body reads as a fragment). The blank-identifier test pins a data-loss guard that has no symptom — the rows would simply overwrite each other. The no-inference test pins the refusal to guess a type.
edits.sketch:
TestValueDefsCoversVarAndConst              // kinds, exported, doc, DECLARED type
TestValueDefsSpansAreSpecLevelInsideABlock  // First's span must not swallow Second
TestValueDefsLoneDeclarationIncludesTheKeyword // slice starts at `var Table`, contains the whole literal
TestValueDefsSkipsBlankIdentifier           // `var _ Iface = …` × 2 ⇒ only Real indexed
TestValueDefsOneEntryPerName                // `var alpha, beta = compute()` ⇒ 2 entries, shared span
TestValueDefsDoesNotInferAType              // `var x = compute()` ⇒ Type == ""

grounded_in: internal/analysis/analyse.go, the defect in one line: the GenDecl case reads `if d.Tok == token.TYPE {` — token.VAR and token.CONST fall through and are never appended to anything.
code_symbols' own constraint, which has permitted these kinds all along: "code_symbols_kind_check" CHECK (kind = ANY (ARRAY['func','method','struct','interface','alias','type','var','const'])).

The reader has expected them all along too: `var codeKindList = []string{"func", "method", "struct", "interface", "alias", "type", "var", "const"}` in diagnose_code_lookup_action.go — the allow-list that decides whether a row renders as CODE or as a [doc] row.

Live census 2026-08-10 (unchanged in composition since the bug was filed): SELECT kind, count(*) FROM code_symbols GROUP BY 1 → func 3653, method 1119, struct 987, alias 42, interface 36. No var, no const, no type row.

bugs_open/223's third failure mode, on a live Go var: 'metaCommentaryPatterns and placeholderPatterns no longer resolve as standalone symbols (possibly inlined or renamed)' — both exist at HEAD, unrenamed, at validate_page_content.go:105 and :1229. 'The phrasing manufactures a hypothesis the evidence never supported.'

bugs_open/223's 2026-08-09 addendum, the second consumer: a 090 run 'stopped at UNVERIFIABLE with this as its stated gap 1: the actual var declaration of DeployImageAssetInputSpec — specifically its Defaults map — is NOT in the bundle. The content search for the identifier only surfaced its two USE sites … never the literal spec definition.' … 'Whoever fixes this bug's lookup layer fixes both consumers at once.'

Corpus growth MEASURED by building the new analyser and running it over this tree, not estimated from grep: var=795 const=576 (1,371 entries) across 811 files. My own earlier grep gave 930 (blind to block members) and an awk estimate gave 1,173; both are superseded by running the parser that will emit the rows.

The prune interlock, read in prune_floor.go rather than assumed: ratio() — 'An empty cohort has nothing to lose, so it reads as fully confirmed rather than as 0/0 — a new class appearing for the first time must never be able to refuse a prune.' So the first run is safe by construction, and the exposure is the reverse (an OLD binary against a DB that already holds var rows sets Allowed=false and refuses the whole prune — safe, self-healing, visible).

Phase 1's own scope statement, kept honest here: 'This does NOT fix the var/const blind spot itself — bugs_open/231's class still stops at UNVERIFIABLE. It now stops honestly, naming the index as the limit instead of inventing a rename. Indexing those kinds is phase 2, its own commit and round.'

Owner ruling 2026-07-29 §1, the test this change is measured against: 'An addition to a shared vocabulary needs an RFC only when it changes what the shared mechanism GUARANTEES.' Filling two kinds already reserved in the constraint, the reader's allow-list and the analyser's stated Go contract makes the existing guarantee true for more of Go; it does not change its direction.
plan.risks:
1. CORPUS GROWTH is the whole risk surface: +1,371 analyser entries (~+20-23% of 5,837, lower in the DB because index_code_symbols excludes paths the analyser sees — 811 files vs 682 indexed). Every diagnosis run's retrieval search space widens accordingly, and a `content` search that previously matched only use sites will now also match declarations. That is the intended effect and it is also a behaviour change every consumer of the index sees, so the consumers are named and told rather than merely measured: fix-proposer, feature-designer, landmine-verifier, and the diagnosis loop's runtime lane.

2. EMBEDDING COST is one-off and bounded: ~1,371 new rows need embedding; existing rows are untouched because content_hash is unchanged for them, so none of the 5,837 existing vectors is recomputed. Embedding failure is already non-fatal and reported by the action.

3. PRUNE, mixed-fleet window: an OLD binary indexing against a DB that already holds var rows reads cohort kind=var at 0% confirmed and REFUSES THE WHOLE PRUNE (evaluatePruneFloor is all-cohorts). Safe direction — nothing is deleted — self-healing on the next run from a new image, and visible in the prune-refusal note. Watch for refusals persisting more than one refresh cycle after the fleet converges on one image.

4. IDENTITY: (repo, path, symbol) admits no new collision — Go forbids two package-level declarations of one name in a package, and method rows are receiver-qualified. The blank identifier IS a collision source and is skipped for that reason; without the skip, every `var _ Iface = (*T)(nil)` in one file would UPSERT over the previous one and all but one would vanish silently.

5. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not ingest non-Go files (still architecture-scope, still excluded), and it does not make bugs_open/231's 090 run succeed by itself — it removes the structural reason that run could not see the declaration. Whether that run then CONFIRMS is a separate question, and the acceptance step is written to check the row and its body exist, not to claim the downstream verdict.

6. NOT YET MEASURABLE, stated rather than guessed: the exact post-index DB counts and the first prune's cohort verdicts. Both need the indexer to run against a rolled image; the acceptance steps name the two queries.
